name: One Key+ Card
effective_cost: Moderate: the $100 anniversary bonus alone covers the $99 fee if you'll use it
balance_transfer_fee: $5 or 5% of each transfer, whichever is greater

welcome_bonus.requirement: after you spend $3,000 in purchases within the first 3 months of account opening

verdict.text: Keep if Gold status and the $100 anniversary bonus beat the $99 fee

earn_note: Same category structure as the free One Key card, with the base rate on everything else raised from 1.5% to 2%. That extra 0.5 points on non-bonused spend is the main earning reason to pay the $99 fee.

redemption_options.method: Book travel on Expedia, Hotels.com, or Vrbo

points.note: OneKeyCash is not redeemable for cash, statement credit, or gift cards; it only spends on Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo, the same closed loop as the free One Key card.

transfer_partners.highlight: No transfer partners. OneKeyCash isn't a transferable currency, it's a closed-loop credit for Expedia, Hotels.com, and Vrbo.

credits.name: Anniversary OneKeyCash Bonus
credits.subtitle: $100 · once per year
credits.description: $100 in OneKeyCash automatically credited to the account every cardmember anniversary, no spending requirement.
tips: Automatic, so it's the one credit on this card that doesn't need any action to collect.

credits.name: Global Entry / TSA PreCheck Credit
credits.subtitle: $120 · every 4 years
credits.description: Statement credit up to $120 every four years after the Global Entry or TSA PreCheck application fee is charged to the card. Shown here amortized to an annual figure.
tips: Apply for Global Entry rather than just TSA PreCheck; it includes TSA PreCheck and covers the same credit.

insurance.detail: Reimbursement for covered cancellations or interruptions on common carrier fares; exact per-trip limit not published on the card's marketing page
Up to $1,000,000 when the full fare for a common carrier ticket is charged to the card
Up to $50,000, secondary coverage that applies after your personal auto insurance
Up to $1,000 per claim against damage or theft when you pay your monthly cell phone bill with this card, minus a $25 deductible, max 2 claims per 12 months
Not responsible for unauthorized transactions once reported

protection_note: The same strong travel insurance suite as the free One Key card (trip cancellation, travel accident, cell phone protection), plus the Global Entry/TSA PreCheck credit this tier adds. Purchase protection and extended warranty still aren't advertised.
rental_note: Secondary coverage up to $50,000, meaning it pays after your personal auto policy for whatever's left, up to that limit. Charge the full rental cost to the card and decline the counter's optional CDW to activate it.

status_perks.name: Gold tier, One Key membership
status_perks.note: Automatic Gold status gives 20% or more in savings on 10,000+ VIP Access hotels booked through Expedia, Hotels.com, or Vrbo. Platinum tier unlocks after $30,000 in annual card spending.

services.name: $350 welcome bonus
services.detail: $350 in OneKeyCash after spending $3,000 in purchases within the first 3 months.

services.name: No foreign transaction fee
services.detail: $0 on purchases made outside the US.

additional_cards.title: Authorized users

benefits.text: Earns OneKeyCash on their spend (into your account)

additional_cards.note: No cost to add, and their spending earns the same category rates into your account.

timeline.text: Wells Fargo issues One Key+ as the premium tier alongside the free One Key card, tied to Expedia Group's unified One Key loyalty program. The exact launch date isn't confirmed here; treat it as approximate.
